title: Mattathias
hookLine: a priest in Modi'in refuses to sacrifice to idols, and the revolt begins

lines: GO FIRST, AND BE THE KING'S FRIEND.
cards: Modi'in is a town, not the capital. The first book of Maccabees says a priest named Mattathias lives there with his five sons: John, Simon, Judas who is called Maccabeus, Eleazar and Jonathan.

He has been mourning what's happening in Jerusalem, tearing his clothes, putting on sackcloth. Then the king's officers come to make the town sacrifice to idols, and they go straight to him, because he's a leader there.
Their offer is friendly: go first, set the example, and you and your sons will be counted among the king's friends, rewarded with silver and gold. Everyone in town is watching.

teach.h: I AND MY SONS WILL WALK IN THE COVENANT.
teach.b: He answers loudly, so the whole crowd hears: even if every nation in the king's realm obeys and abandons the ways of its ancestors, I and my sons and my brothers will walk in the covenant of our fathers.
Then the story turns violent. Another Jew steps up to offer the sacrifice.
Mattathias, burning with zeal, kills him at the altar, kills the king's officer too, and pulls the altar down. The book compares him to Phinehas, the zealous priest in Numbers.
It's a hard scene, and some readers are uneasy with it; the book offers no apology.
Then Mattathias calls through the town for anyone zealous for the law and faithful to the covenant to follow him, and he and his sons flee to the mountains, leaving everything.
Some later Hanukkah retellings put an older cry in his mouth, the call Moses made at the golden calf.

teach.h: WHO IS ON THE LORD'S SIDE?
teach.b: In the King James words: "Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me." In Hebrew, mi la-Adonai elai. Then a turn that's easy to miss.
Some of the faithful hide in the wilderness, the enemy attacks them on the Sabbath, and they refuse even to block the caves. They die, the text says, with their families.
When Mattathias hears, he and his friends decide: if anyone attacks us on the Sabbath, we will fight back, or we'll all be wiped out.
Refusing the king also meant choosing to stay alive, so the covenant would still have people to keep it.

how: At Hanukkah, Jews add the Al HaNissim passage to their prayers, which names Mattathias son of Yohanan, the Hasmonean high priest, and his sons.

o: the high priest who later rededicated the Temple
the priest of Modi'in who refused and began the revolt
the king's officer sent to Modi'in to enforce the ban

p: go first and be counted his friend
the zealous priest he's compared to

s: Mattathias lived in Jerusalem when the officers came
1 Maccabees places him in Modi'in, a town where the officers came to enforce the sacrifice.
the faithful in the caves first refused to fight on the Sabbath
they would not even block the caves, and died; then Mattathias and his friends decided to fight back if attacked.

games.q: you're Mattathias. the king's officers offer you silver, gold and the king's friendship if you sacrifice first, with the whole town watching. what do you say?
o: go first, quietly, and keep your faith inside.
even if every nation obeys, I and my sons will walk in the covenant.
send one of your sons to do it instead.
games.why: he answers out loud that he and his family will keep the covenant, then calls the faithful to follow him into the mountains.

practice: Think of one small wrong you're being invited to join, a rumor at work, a joke at somebody's expense, a shortcut that cheats someone, and picture the moment the invitation comes, with everyone watching.
Hear yourself say no, calmly, in one short sentence, until it feels like yours. If you pray, ask in words from your tradition for steadiness.

wordCard.voice: Mattathias. The priest of Modi'in who refused the king's sacrifice, called the faithful to follow, and began the revolt. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: whoever is for the Lord, to me. Moses's call in Exodus 32:26, which some later Hanukkah retellings give to Mattathias.

carryVoice: Your line: who is for the lord. He said no aloud, with the whole town watching. Day eight hundred ninety-two.
